body_markdown:
Running several payment providers is more useful when the payments team can control routing and see the results together.[Razorpay Optimizer](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/optimizer/) combines configurable routing rules, real-time performance signals and consolidated visibility of payments, refunds and settlements. For a business using Razorpay that wants to manage supported providers through that integration, Optimizer is a natural choice for payment orchestration.


## Key takeaways


- Shape routing around payment method, bank, card type, issuer and transaction amount, using the controls documented for your setup.
- Review successful payments and costs over a consistent period to assess the results of routing decisions.
- Activate Optimizer and configure credentials for onboarded, supported providers. Confirm each provider-and-method combination, especially for international transactions.


## What Razorpay Optimizer does


The[Optimizer documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/optimizer/) describes rules based on payment method, bank, card type, issuer and transaction amount. These controls let the payments team shape routing around its customer mix and commercial agreements, then compare successful payments and costs over a consistent period. The benefit is a configurable payment workflow whose results the business can assess.


Activate Optimizer and configure credentials for the supported providers you have onboarded. Confirm the provider-and-method combination before rollout, especially for international transactions.


## When to evaluate routing


Begin with evidence from your existing payment flow. Separate failures caused by a technical issue, an unavailable provider, customer abandonment, issuer decisions and other causes. Match each failure category to the routing or customer-support action that can address it.


Evaluate routing when the supported alternative paths and configuration could address a material part of your observed failures. Consider the additional commercial, reconciliation, engineering and operational work.


Transaction volume, failure patterns, payment mix and implementation cost help estimate the potential value of routing. Discuss these factors with Razorpay when confirming eligibility and the right configuration.


## Compare building and adopting a routing layer


Decision area Question to resolve


Supported paths Which providers, methods and checkout platforms can the intended configuration use?


Integration What account activation and provider configuration are required?


Failure handling Which failures can the documented flow handle, and which need another action?


Operations How will the team monitor routing, reconcile payments and investigate exceptions?


Cost What processing and optional-product charges apply?


Measurement How will the team compare outcomes on equivalent payment traffic?


## Implement a controlled evaluation


1. Measure the current payment mix and failure reasons.
2. Review the[Optimizer documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/optimizer) and supported configuration.
3. Request activation and confirm the commercial terms.
4. Configure the approved payment paths and rules.
5. Test success, failure, duplicate-prevention and reconciliation behaviour in the documented integration.
6. Run a controlled rollout and compare equivalent traffic where possible.
7. Monitor payment success, latency, cost and operational exceptions together.


Use the documented routing and retry behaviour for each payment method. Classify failure reasons so your team can distinguish payment-path issues from cases requiring customer action, issuer approval or account review.


## Measure routing performance for your business


Define the success-rate denominator before the evaluation. Keep payment method, customer mix, period and traffic allocation comparable, and record outages or other changes that could affect the result.


Use a documented baseline and comparable traffic to measure the results achieved in your configuration. This gives your team a reliable basis for deciding whether to expand the rollout.


## Frequently asked questions


### Does a business need a fixed monthly turnover before evaluating Optimizer?


Discuss eligibility with Razorpay and evaluate the opportunity using your payment mix, routing requirements, cost and implementation effort. The public overview does not specify a universal turnover threshold.


### Is Optimizer enabled automatically for every account?


Optimizer is available on demand. Request activation and confirm the configuration and commercial terms for your account.


### Which payment failures can routing help address?


Routing can help with payment-path issues where another supported route is available. Review the failure cause and supported configuration; issuer decisions, customer authorisation and account restrictions require their appropriate resolution.


### Is routing included in a standard processing rate?


Use the product-specific commercial terms for Optimizer alongside your processing rates when calculating the total cost.
